anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
**(1) First message**

The framing holds. I checked the reports page, which renders a table and has no export action. I checked `src/export/csv.ts`, which already builds its output from the table's column definitions, so the serializer can be reused. I checked the ticket's repo groups against this repo: overrides `## Issue tracker` says `repo: acme/widgets`. I also traced the 10k-row/60s row's implicit dependencies, which are paged data access and a 10k-row report to time against. These checks come from the gather draft's trace. I have not re-read `src/export/csv.ts` or the reports page source this turn, so I will verify both before spec-writing.

Here is the status of each premise:

- **Supported:** No export action exists today, and the existing CSV serializer works from the table's column definitions. Source: the gather draft's `Pattern:` line on `src/export/csv.ts`.
- **Corrected:** The 60s row assumes the data layer can return 10k rows in bounded chunks. It cannot, because paging is unimplemented. The design therefore has to add paging rather than rely on it.
- **Unverified:** Nobody has measured whether 10k rows can export in under 60s. There is also no evidence that the target is impossible, so the row stays `in-scope`. The design will carry a timing test, and the achieved time goes in Open Questions until it is measured.
- **Not checkable yet:** There is no 10k-row report to run that test against. Neither the gather draft nor the ticket names a seed or fixture, and I found none to cite. The timing test will need a generated 10k-row fixture.

I am making two assumptions:

- The row `Exports are emailed to the requesting user.` sits under the `acme/mailer` group, which is not this repo. It is recorded as `elsewhere: acme/mailer`.
- The other three rows under `acme/widgets` are `in-scope` as written.

Where should the Export CSV button appear on the reports page?
A) Beside the report title
B) In the table's header/toolbar row, above the columns
C) Inside a page-level actions menu
D) other - name it
Recommendation: A - a single page-level action is most discoverable next to the title, and it needs no new menu.

---

**(2) Approaches message**

Two implicit dependencies remain before the approaches:

- **Paging:** The 10k-row timing row depends on fetching report rows in bounded chunks. The gather trace found paging unimplemented, so that dependency is missing and any approach that meets the row must add it.
- **A 10k-row report:** The timing test needs one. Neither the repo nor the ticket names a fixture or seed, so it is not checkable today. The test will generate one.

The approaches differ on one axis: where the 10k rows are gathered and serialized. The options are paged fetches feeding the existing serializer, the rows the table already holds, or a new server-side stream.

**Recommended - A) Reuse the CSV serializer, add paging to the report data fetch.**
The button loops over paged fetches of the report. It feeds each page to `src/export/csv.ts`, using the visible table columns in table order, and downloads the result. This is the only option that meets the 10k/60s row without loading everything into the table at once. It also keeps one serializer and one column source. The trade-off is that adding paging touches the report data fetch, which every report caller shares. That is a wider blast radius, and the existing callers' behavior needs a regression test.
Removes: none
Adds: page/cursor parameters on the report data fetch; an Export CSV button beside the title; an export handler that loops pages into `src/export/csv.ts`; a timing test with a generated 10k-row fixture; a column-parity test
Pattern: follows `src/export/csv.ts`'s use of the table's column definitions as the single column source. Paging is added on the owning fetch, not as a parallel loader.

**B) Reuse-only: serialize the rows the table already holds.**
The button passes the table's in-memory rows and visible columns straight to `src/export/csv.ts`, with no paging. It is the smallest change and adds no data-layer work. However, the table only holds what it loaded. Without paging, a 10k-row report means either the page already loads all 10k rows, which I cannot confirm, or the export is truncated. Either way the 60s row is unproven.
Removes: none
Adds: an Export CSV button; a handler calling `src/export/csv.ts` with table rows and columns
Pattern: follows `src/export/csv.ts`. It ties export completeness to the page's own loading behavior, which the ticket's 10k-row row does not allow for.

**C) Drop the client-built assumption: a server-side streaming CSV endpoint.**
The button hits an endpoint that pages the query on the server and streams rows through the same serializer. This approach scales best. Its cost is a new route, and the serializer has to run server-side. It also adds a second export boundary beside the client table, which the ask does not need for 10k rows.
Removes: none
Adds: a CSV export route; server-side paging over the report query; a button linking to the route; timing and column-parity tests
Pattern: reuses `src/export/csv.ts`, but adds a new server boundary for one caller.

I recommend A. It meets every `acme/widgets` row with one serializer and one column source, and it adds paging where the data is owned. That recommendation would flip to C if the timing test shows paged client fetches cannot finish 10k rows in under 60s.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.text:
## 1. First message to the user

The framing holds on the supplied evidence: the draft describes a reports table without an export action and identifies `src/export/csv.ts` as an existing serializer using table column definitions. I cannot independently verify the report’s callers, loading path, column-selection behavior, or serializer contract without tools; those remain unverified rather than established code facts.

The design will retain all three `acme/widgets` acceptance criteria, including exporting a 10k-row report in under 60 seconds. Missing paging does not establish that the performance target is impossible, so it is not grounds for cutting that requirement. The email-delivery row belongs to `acme/mailer` and will be recorded as `elsewhere: acme/mailer`.

Where should the Export CSV button appear?
A) Beside the report title.
B) In the table toolbar.
C) Other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it makes exporting discoverable as a report-level action.

## 2. Approaches message

Using your recorded answers, the button belongs beside the report title, and the export must use the visible table columns in table order.

The draft reports that paging is missing; the report-loading implementation and available paging API remain unverified because no primary-code lookup is available. The serializer’s handling of column visibility, ordering, and multiple batches is also unverified: the only supplied location is `src/export/csv.ts`. The under-60-second target remains binding but unmeasured.

**I recommend reusing the existing CSV serializer and adding paging.** The meaningful choice is whether to collect the report before serialization or introduce incremental export orchestration.

### A) Collect paged rows, then serialize using the existing path — recommended

Extend the report-loading path to retrieve the complete report page by page, then pass the collected rows and the visible, ordered column definitions to the existing serializer. This minimizes new export machinery and keeps CSV formatting in its existing owner.

The trade-off is retaining the complete report in memory before producing the download. Performance must be measured with a 10k-row report; this approach does not itself prove the 60-second requirement.

Removes: none.
Adds: report-title export button and action wiring; paging behavior in the report-loading path; complete-report collection; visible-column selection passed to the existing serializer; tests for placement, columns, paging completeness, and the performance requirement.
Pattern: Reuses the CSV-formatting owner identified in `src/export/csv.ts`; the shared loader’s callers and the impact of extending it still require verification.

### B) Page and serialize incrementally

Introduce an export coordinator that retrieves pages and serializes them incrementally, reusing the existing serializer’s formatting behavior. This can reduce retained row data, but adds coordination around headers, page order, partial failures, and output assembly. Whether it helps depends on the serializer and download mechanisms, neither of which has been inspected.

Removes: none.
Adds: report-title export button and action wiring; paged export coordinator; incremental output assembly; any necessary batch support in the existing serializer; visible-column selection; tests for placement, columns, paging completeness, batch boundaries, failures, and performance.
Pattern: Keeps formatting with `src/export/csv.ts`, but introduces a separate orchestration boundary that needs justification over extending the existing loading path.

An assumption-dropping candidate would avoid paging and request the entire report at once. It is not currently a grounded implementation option: the supplied observations identify no complete-report retrieval API. Likewise, exporting only already-loaded rows is not a safe reuse-only substitute for exporting a complete 10k-row report.

Your recorded choice selects **A: reuse the existing serializer and add paging**. I would revisit incremental orchestration only if code inspection or measurement shows that collecting the report first cannot meet the approved requirements.
